claim: A managed write replaces only the content between the exact markers — everything outside them survives byte for byte, and generated content carrying a marker of its own is refused rather than written.

steps.label: the agent rewrites its own block

request.document: human text + managed block + human text

steps.result:
# Toy Repository

Hand-written by a person.   
<!-- BEGIN MANAGED BLOCK -->
generated v2
<!-- END MANAGED BLOCK -->
## Notes
	still hand-written
steps.evidence: text above and below the markers is the original bytes, CRLF endings and trailing spaces included
steps.note: Rewriting the whole file is the usual approach, and it silently normalizes exactly this.

steps.label: generated content carrying a start marker

request.new content:
sneaky
<!-- BEGIN MANAGED BLOCK -->
second block

steps.detail: generated content carries a managed-block marker
steps.evidence: the file was never opened — the render is pure and refused first
steps.note: Two start markers means no single managed region, and every later edit would have to guess which one the agent owns.

steps.label: generated content carrying an end marker

request.new content:
<!-- END MANAGED BLOCK -->
and then text pretending to be human

steps.detail: generated content carries a managed-block marker
steps.note: The inverse trick: escape the block and write below it.

steps.label: a document that already contains two blocks
steps.note: Ambiguity fails closed. Absence does not — a document with no block yet is legal, and the block is created without moving anything.

steps.note: A re-run is a no-op, not a slow accumulation of blocks.
